title: How GPT-2 small picks the indirect object (IOI)
label: verified (local-full, full precision)
behavior: Given 'When Mary and John went to the store, John gave a drink to', GPT-2 small (local-full, fp32) continues with the non-repeated name (' Mary'). Baseline on ioi seed 0: accuracy 0.94, mean logit diff (IO - S) 3.77 (E0002).
summary: The model works out which name to output by spotting which name is repeated, then copying the other one. (1) At the second mention of the subject (S2), early heads notice the repeat: 3.0 attends from S2 back to the earlier copy S1, and 5.5 attends to the token right after S1, induction-style. 6.9 and some supporting heads (0.1, 1.11, 5.8, 4.3, 5.9, 6.0) help. (2) Layer 7-8 heads 7.3, 7.9, 8.6 and 8.10 attend from the final token (END) to S2 and carry the signal 'this name was repeated' to END. Residual patching shows the handoff from S2 to END happening across layers 7-8. (3) This signal sets the queries of the name-mover heads 9.9, 9.6 and 10.0. Those heads attend from END to the non-repeated name and write it into the logits (9.9 alone contributes +3.0 directly). Their attention target flips when the other name is repeated, so it follows repetition, not position. (4) Heads 10.7 and 11.10 attend to the same name but write against it, which damps the answer. Removing the name movers costs little because backup heads in layers 9-11 take over. The upstream repeat signal is the real bottleneck: ablating the four S2 readers leaves only 12% of the logit diff. The 23 heads plus mlp0-6 passed held-out verification (V0002).
pseudocode:
def predict(tokens, prompt):
    names = capitalised words after 'When'      # A, B, ..., C
    first_two, later = names[:2], names[2:]
    # Stage 1 @S2 (E0009, E0012, E0024): heads 3.0 (S2->S1), 5.5 (S2->S1+1), 6.9 mark S2's name as already seen
    repeated = [n for n in first_two if n in later]
    # Stage 2 @END (E0005, E0008, E0011, E0023): 7.3, 7.9, 8.6, 8.10 read S2 and set name-mover queries
    # Stage 3 @END (E0008, E0010, E0020): 9.9, 9.6, 10.0 attend to the non-repeated name and copy it to the logits
    #   10.7, 11.10 attend to the same name and write against it (E0010, E0014); backups in layers 9-11 (E0016, E0019)
    candidates = [n for n in first_two if n not in repeated]
    return ' ' + (candidates[0] if candidates else first_two[0])

claims.text: GPT-2 small does the task: accuracy 0.94, logit diff IO-S 3.77 on ioi seed 0 (local-full).

With a corruption that changes only which name is repeated, the information sits at S2 up to layer 7 and moves to END across layers 7-8 (END recovery 0.32 at resid_pre.8, 0.91 at resid_pre.9; S2 recovery 0.91 at layer 7, 0.06 at layer 9).
Heads 3.0 (S2->S1, 0.77) and 5.5 (S2->S1+1, 0.85) attend from the repeated name back to its earlier occurrence. They, together with 6.9, are the main senders into the values of the S2-reader heads.

Heads 7.9, 8.6 and 8.10 attend from END to S2, and 7.3 attends to S2+1. These four are the only significant senders into the queries of name movers 9.9, 9.6 and 10.0 (path effects 0.05-0.16; every other head < 0.05).
9.9 and 9.6 attend from END to the non-repeated name and write it directly into the logits (DLA +3.0 and +1.2). Their attention target flips from pos 2 to pos 4 when the repeated name changes.
10.7 and 11.10 attend to the same IO name but write against it (DLA -2.0, -0.8). Ablating either one raises the logit diff (+1.43, +0.77).

Name movers are redundant: jointly ablating 9.9, 9.6, 10.0, 10.10 and 10.6 keeps 83% of the logit diff, and also ablating 10.7 and 11.10 still keeps 79%. Ablating all attention in layers 9-11 leaves 20%, so backup capacity is spread across layers 9, 10 and 11.
The repeat signal is the bottleneck: ablating the S2 readers alone leaves 12% of the logit diff, and ablating readers plus duplicate heads leaves 10%.

MLPs carry little task-specific information except mlp0, which processes the S2 token (patching recovery 0.89). mlp1-6 are nevertheless needed as general infrastructure for the circuit to work on its own, while mlp7-11 are not.

Held-out verification (seed 777, n=200, local-full): predict() agrees with the model on 93.5% of prompts, and every disagreement is the model choosing a non-name token. Ablating the circuit drops the logit diff to -13% of clean. Keeping only the circuit preserves 99% of the logit diff, but top-1 accuracy falls to 0.375. Random ablations of the same size keep 104-106%.
With all MLPs intact, ablating only the 23 circuit heads reverses the preference (logit diff -1.48).
The first 15-component circuit (14 heads + mlp0) failed sufficiency (circuit alone -10%). Adding nine supporting heads and mlp1-6 fixed it.

limitations: All numbers come from local-full (fp32) on one template family ('When A and B went to the P, C gave a O to'). Other IOI templates were not tested.
The circuit alone keeps 99% of the logit diff but only 0.375 top-1 accuracy (V0002). It explains the choice of IO over S, not the full drive to output a name instead of ' the'/' her'.

mlp1-6 are in the verified circuit as general infrastructure (E0028 vs E0029); I did not find a task-specific role for them (E0021). The task-specific necessity of the heads is shown separately (E0030).
The nine supporting heads (0.1, 1.11, 4.3, 4.11, 5.8, 5.9, 6.0, 9.7, 10.1) were added because of small effects in earlier experiments. Each one's role was not characterised individually.
Backup name movers were located only by layer (E0016, E0018, E0019), not identified individually. DLA under ablation is unsupported (E0017 ignored the parameter).

The edges from duplicate heads to individual S2 readers in the diagram are drawn at group level: E0012 measured senders into all four readers jointly, and E0011 measured senders into the three name movers jointly.
In the IO-first prompts, 9.7 and 10.0 attend mostly to BOS from END (E0008), yet 10.0 writes +0.74 directly. How it does that is unexplained.
E0025 (what feeds 5.5's keys) was inconclusive by design, so the previous-token feed into 5.5 is not established.
open_questions: Which individual heads in layers 9-11 act as backups when the main name movers are ablated, and do they read the same S2-reader signal?
Does 5.5 rely on a previous-token head (e.g. 4.11) at S1+1? This needs a corruption that changes S1 while keeping S2 matched.
What exactly do the S2 readers write: a positional signal, a name-identity signal, or both? This could be probed with linear_probe / diff_of_means at END in layer 9.
Why do 10.7 and 11.10 copy IO negatively, and do they respond to how strongly the name movers wrote?
Does the circuit carry over to other IOI templates and to longer contexts?
overall_status: partial / not verified · verified (local-full, full precision)
